provider: Gmail (free @gmail.com) — 15 GB shared, and the honest ceiling of 'Gmail as infinite storage'

free_tier.stated: 15 GB per Google Account, shared across Gmail, Drive and Photos: "Each Google Account includes up to 15 GB of storage, which is shared across Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos." Attachments: 25 MB send ("For personal Gmail accounts, the limit is 25 MB"), 50 MB receive.

egress.terms: Free for the account holder — Gmail has no egress meter at all; the constraint is the bandwidth throttle, not a price. That is precisely why the throttle is the finding.

tooling: IMAP probe-verified: `imap.gmail.com:993` -> `* OK Gimap ready` / `* CAPABILITY IMAP4rev1 UNSELECT IDLE NAMESPACE QUOTA ID XLIST CHILDREN X-GM-EXT-1 XYZZY SASL-IR AUTH=XOAUTH2 AUTH=PLAIN AUTH=PLAIN-CLIENTTOKEN AUTH=OAUTHBEARER` (XOAUTH2 required for real use). Gmail API: `messages.insert` = 25 units, 6,000 units/min/user, 80,000,000 units/day/project.
chaining: N accounts × 15 GB minus whatever Drive/Photos already took. But the multiplier that matters is not accounts — see limits. This is the classic 'infinite Gmail storage' idea and it does not survive arithmetic.
limits_note: SMTP advertises `250-SIZE 35882577` (34.2 MiB) per message. So per account the real write rate is ~0.5 GB/day and the real read rate is ~2.5 GB/day. Filling 15 GB therefore takes a **minimum of ~30 days per account**, and serving 500 GB/day of reads requires **~200 accounts running in parallel every day**. Gmail is not a fetch tier by two orders of magnitude. To reach 10 TiB of writes you would need 20,480 account-days of upload. Verdict on the idea: 15 GB × unlimited accounts is arithmetically true and operationally false — the daily byte meter, not the quota, is the wall.
reliability_note: Exceeding the bandwidth limit suspends IMAP upload for ~1 hour (up to 24 h); repeated heavy sync is the documented trigger, and the docs explicitly call out 'syncing a Gmail account to a third-party email client' as a cause.
